scenes.title: A book about making friends
scenes.titleZh: 找一本教人交朋友的书
scenes.summary: A librarian offers science books; Sheldon asks for help making a friend, and she finds a book for him.
scenes.practice: Asking for help, offering suggestions, responding with dry humour.
scenes.contentNotes: A child feels out of place at school; the librarian makes a self-deprecating joke about being unpopular.
scenes.reviewStatus: draft-source-and-boundary-reviewed; human listening and age-fit review pending

lines.speaker: Librarian
lines.text: Hey there, Sheldon. What can I get for you today? Chemistry? Quantum mechanics? Astronomy?
lines.hint: 嗨，谢尔顿。今天想找什么？化学？量子力学？天文学？

lines.speaker: Sheldon
lines.text: No, nothing fun today. I need to learn how to make a friend.
lines.hint: 不，今天不找有趣的东西。我得学学怎么交朋友。

lines.speaker: Librarian
lines.text: Oh, honey. You having a hard time adjusting to high school?
lines.hint: 哦，亲爱的。你还不太适应高中吗？

lines.speaker: Sheldon
lines.text: I'm having a hard time adjusting to Earth.
lines.hint: 我还不太适应地球。

lines.speaker: Librarian
lines.text: Yeah, you and me both.
lines.hint: 是啊，咱俩都一样。

lines.speaker: Librarian
lines.text: Try this. It's been around a while, but it's still quite popular. Unlike me, who's just been around a while.
lines.hint: 试试这本。它出版很久了，但依然很受欢迎。不像我，只有年头长。

scenes.title: Trying out a book’s advice
scenes.summary: Sheldon repeatedly uses his father’s name and asks whether the technique is working; George points out that he is overdoing it.
scenes.practice: Questions, feedback and playful disagreement.
scenes.contentNotes: Family sarcasm. The cut ends after the final name repetition and before the channel end card.
scenes.reviewStatus: draft-source-and-boundary-reviewed; human listening and age-fit review pending

lines.speaker: Sheldon
lines.text: Do you feel complimented when I say your name, George? The book says you should. George.
lines.hint: 我叫你的名字时，你觉得受到赞美了吗，乔治？书上说你会的。乔治。

lines.speaker: George Cooper Sr.
lines.text: I suppose. Kind of overdoing it a little. Sheldon.
lines.hint: 算是吧。你有点做过头了。谢尔顿。

lines.speaker: Sheldon
lines.text: Well, thank you for your criticism. It also says I should praise any improvements that you've made.
lines.hint: 谢谢你的批评。书上还说，我应该表扬你的进步。

lines.speaker: George Cooper Sr.
lines.text: Okay.
lines.hint: 好啊。

lines.speaker: Sheldon
lines.text: I'll get back to you. George.
lines.hint: 有了我再告诉你。乔治。

scenes.title: Asking Dad to talk to a teacher
scenes.summary: Sheldon explains a difficult assignment and tries several arguments to persuade his father to speak to his professor.
scenes.practice: Explaining a problem, requests, reasons and refusal.
scenes.contentNotes: College homework is the setting; the selected exchange uses parent/child language. Mild criticism of the professor. Later crude adult dialogue is excluded.
scenes.reviewStatus: draft-source-and-boundary-reviewed; human listening and age-fit review pending

lines.speaker: George Cooper Sr.
lines.text: What's going on?
lines.hint: 怎么了？

lines.speaker: Sheldon
lines.text: I can't figure out this engineering project, and every time I turn it in, my professor just rips it up.
lines.hint: 我做不明白这个工程作业，每次交上去，教授都直接把它撕了。

lines.speaker: George Cooper Sr.
lines.text: Well, ain't this the fella you liked?
lines.hint: 这不是你挺喜欢的那个老师吗？

lines.speaker: Sheldon
lines.text: I did when I thought he was pushing me to be all I could be, but it turns out all he can be is mean.
lines.hint: 我以为他在激发我的潜能时是挺喜欢他。结果他只会刻薄。

lines.speaker: George Cooper Sr.
lines.text: I'm sure you'll figure it out.
lines.hint: 你肯定能想明白的。

lines.speaker: Sheldon
lines.text: Could you talk to him?
lines.hint: 你能跟他谈谈吗？

lines.speaker: George Cooper Sr.
lines.text: You're in college now. Don't you think you should fight your own battles?
lines.hint: 你都上大学了，不该自己解决问题了吗？

lines.speaker: Sheldon
lines.text: Does telling on him to the president of the university count?
lines.hint: 那向大学校长告状算不算？

lines.speaker: George Cooper Sr.
lines.text: Did it work?
lines.hint: 管用了吗？

lines.speaker: Sheldon
lines.text: No.
lines.hint: 没有。

lines.speaker: George Cooper Sr.
lines.text: Then no.
lines.hint: 那就不算。

lines.speaker: Sheldon
lines.text: Will you please talk to him?
lines.hint: 拜托你跟他谈谈好吗？

lines.speaker: George Cooper Sr.
lines.text: What if your mom does it?
lines.hint: 让你妈妈去怎么样？

lines.speaker: Sheldon
lines.text: But you were both in the army, and you're both crabby and impatient. There's a lot of common ground.
lines.hint: 可你们都当过兵，都脾气暴躁、没耐心。共同点可多了。

scenes.title: Joey discovers a thesaurus
scenes.summary: Joey wants his recommendation to sound smarter; Ross demonstrates a tool, and Joey proudly tries the alternatives.

lines.text: Oh, Monica and Chandler's recommendation. I want it to sound smart, but I don't know any big words or anything, so...
lines.hint: 给莫妮卡和钱德勒写推荐信。我想写得有水平，可我不认识什么高级词汇，所以……

scenes.title: A very nervous driving lesson

scenes.title: Which animal is the better comparison?
scenes.summary: Marshall uses an animal comparison for changing feelings about someone; the group disputes which animal should represent liking someone.
scenes.practice: Opinions, comparisons, disagreement and emphasis.
scenes.contentNotes: A bar setting with drinks, a dating metaphor and a mild insult directed at ducks. Stops before the narrator and later animal-fighting suggestion.
scenes.reviewStatus: draft-source-and-boundary-reviewed; human listening and age-fit review pending

lines.speaker: Marshall
lines.text: Relationships are like that. I mean, look, when you first met Don, you hated him. You thought, this guy's a duck. But one of these days, you're gonna realize this is actually someone that I love. He's a rabbit.
lines.hint: 关系就是这样。你刚认识唐时很讨厌他，觉得他像只鸭子。但总有一天，你会发现自己喜欢他。他其实是只兔子。

lines.speaker: Ted
lines.text: Whoa, I think you got it backwards there, buddy. The duck is the thing you love. The rabbit is the thing you hate.
lines.hint: 等等，老兄，你说反了吧。鸭子是你喜欢的，兔子才是你讨厌的。

lines.speaker: Marshall
lines.text: What?
lines.hint: 什么？

lines.speaker: Robin
lines.text: Yeah, I gotta agree. Ducks up, rabbits down.
lines.hint: 对，我同意。鸭子好，兔子差。

lines.speaker: Lily
lines.text: Definitely. Ducks are better than rabbits.
lines.hint: 绝对的，鸭子比兔子好。

lines.speaker: Marshall
lines.text: Hey, I got... ducks are, ducks are... Rabbits are adorable! Ducks are... Have you ever been in a fight with a duck? I mean, ducks are jerks!
lines.hint: 鸭子……兔子多可爱啊！鸭子嘛……你们跟鸭子打过架吗？我是说，鸭子可讨厌了！
